title: How to call from a different number: 4 business phone apps

##


How to call from a different number with a second SIM


Dual-SIM phones allow you to use two phone numbers by holding two different SIM cards. This option is good for keeping work and personal calls separate on the same device. However, if your cell phone doesn’t support the use of two SIM cards, you’ll need to swap them whenever you want to use your second number. This can be inconvenient, especially when managing calls on the go.


Alternatively, you can use an eSIM, which lets you[add a business line to your cell phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/add-business-line-to-cell-phone/) without a physical SIM card. All you need is a phone like the iPhone XS or newer, along with a carrier that supports eSIM Carrier Activation. Most Android phones sold in the past few years come with a dual SIM slot. Android manufacturers have also made it easy to add eSIMs.


The drawback with dual SIM and eSIM second numbers? You can’t share them with a team. They also lack business-friendly features like CRM integrations, automated texting, or AI-powered automations. They operate just like your personal number, which isn’t ideal for business teams that want to scale quickly.

If your primary goal for a second phone number is verification, an eSIM is a more reliable choice. Banks, rideshare apps, and some social platforms check whether a phone number is registered to a mobile carrier as a fraud prevention measure. Virtual numbers are easy to acquire and are more vulnerable to scammers.

##


Is it really legal to call from a different number?


**Yes, a second number that your business owns is legal to use.** Businesses purchase multiple numbers for different teams to communicate with their customers. Getting a second number from a provider and using it for work calls is no different from having a desk phone.


**Manipulating your phone number and your outbound caller ID isn’t legal.** According to the[FCC](https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/spoofing) : “Spoofing is when a caller deliberately falsifies the information transmitted to your caller ID display to disguise their identity.”


VoIP phone providers like Quo are legitimate entities that issue a real, registered phone number. Spoofing tools let you enter an arbitrary number you do not control. The tell is whether the service issues you a number or lets you type one in.


##


Pro Tip: Want to hide your personal caller ID when you call a business?


If you want to hide your caller ID when you call a business from your personal cell number, you can also dial *67 before your phone number. This withholds your caller ID rather than replacing it.


However, this approach doesn’t work for businesses. Most people decline calls that don’t show a caller ID. You’re better off getting a different number and customizing your caller ID instead of masking your caller ID entirely.
